source.title: Rolling Ball Optimizer: Learning by ironing out loss landscape wrinkles
source.authors: Mohammed D. Belgoumri; Mohamed Reda Bouadjenek; Hakim Hacid; Imran Razzak; Sunil Aryal

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including its conclusion and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains image classifiers and reports training loss and accuracy for RBO and three comparator optimizers. Its short, ten-epoch runs give mixed training results relevant to V1, but the reported accuracy is not training classification error and the paper does not test random or corrupted labels.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports validation performance, not training results. Figure 3 and Figures 4a–4b report training curves, but provide no exact training-error values in the text; the stated comparison is that RBO has lower training loss and higher training accuracy than the other evaluated optimizers. The cited work in the introduction and references is not this paper's own evidence.
record.test_reason: The paper reports its own SGD training-accuracy curves for convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, which bear on V1. However, the supplied text does not preserve readable curve values, and ten-epoch optimizer comparisons do not establish eventual convergence or failure to reach near-zero training error. This is not evidence against V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record largely captures the authors' claims: RBO improves training curves and convergence measured in epochs and permits larger learning rates. Their conclusion also emphasizes substantially greater computational expense, errors from approximate inner optimization, an unproved general ironing conjecture and the need for further realistic evaluation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares a new rolling-ball optimizer against SGD, Entropy-SGD and SAM; it uses 10-epoch image-classification runs and reports training curves, rather than testing the claim's stated convergence recipes or random-label settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The radius and learning rate affect RBO behavior; the paper reports validation accuracy varying with both and divergence for a stated large-radius/learning-rate pair.

fits_no_version.finding: RBO reportedly attains better training accuracy and loss in fewer epochs than SGD, SAM and Entropy-SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RBO improves training progress per epoch over these comparator recipes in the tested ten-epoch image-classification runs.

fits_no_version.finding: An MNIST MLP trained with RBO remains stable at some learning rates up to 100, while radius 30 with learning rate 100 diverges.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RBO stability depends on its radius and learning rate. These results do not measure V5's stability threshold or curvature dynamics.

record.problems: Training curves are figure-only and no exact training classification-error values are stated. Runs last 10 epochs. The authors note that RBO hyperparameters were not tuned and that further experimental evaluation is needed for realistic scenarios.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible optimizer-specific training-curve rows beyond R1–R4. Table 1 is validation performance and does not measure the training behavior in V1.

untested.parts: Eventual convergence with sufficient training; corrupted or random labels; Adam; controlled model-size comparisons; effects of early stopping or regularization. Random initialization is not specified.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious-minimum frequencies and extra student neurons.
Controlled depth comparisons, identity-shortcut interventions and special initialization recipes.
Activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and trainable depth.
Initial linearized stability thresholds, catapult dynamics, curvature trajectories and full-batch edge-of-stability behavior.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V1 limits_scope label: unreadable endpoints and superiority of another optimizer do not demonstrate a limitation of V1. Training accuracy does measure training classification error through its complement; the problem is unavailable values and insufficient convergence evidence. Table 1 reports held-out performance and cannot supply training-error values.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-100 training error explicitly in prose; random or corrupted labels; model-size thresholds; early stopping or regularized recipes; or whether smaller models leave substantial training error.
